items.review_rationale: Read higher-categorical 2-fibre-product universality and connected it to the existing (2,1)-category and 2-finality meanings, retaining pseudocone data.

references.matching_note: All 2-morphisms in the ambient higher category are invertible.

references.context: Higher category theory: coherence isomorphism of 1-morphisms defining a pseudocone
references.reason: The coherence 2-cell is additional data for a pseudo-pullback.

references.context: Higher category theory: pseudocone over a span in a (2,1)-category
references.reason: The maps and coherence arrow form a cone, not necessarily a universal object.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the final-object condition of a (2,1)-category without collapsing it into ordinary 1-category terminality.

references.context: Higher category theory: 1-cell from any object to a final object
references.reason: Existence of 1-cells is part of the higher-categorical finality condition.

references.context: Higher category theory: contractible Hom-groupoid in a (2,1)-category
references.reason: Unique comparison 2-cells characterize finality, not ordinary terminality.

references.disposition: The special (2,1)-categorical final-object property is the meaning being defined; ordinary 1-category finality is not its dependency.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed universal-map Stone–Čech compactification through topological continuity, compactness and Hausdorffness, retaining its source-specific factorization requirement.

references.matching_note: The source has an arbitrary topology.
Both η and the universal extension maps are continuous.
The compact Hausdorff target has the open-cover compactness property.
The target also satisfies the Hausdorff separation condition.

references.phrase: factors uniquely through a continuous map
references.context: Topology: universal mapping property for compact Hausdorff targets
references.reason: The unique extension condition does not itself assert a dense embedding of every source X.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed field norm by determinant of multiplication as a linear map of finite-dimensional extensions.

references.matching_note: Field norm uses a finite-dimensional field extension.
Multiplication by α defines a K-linear endomorphism.

references.context: Linear algebra: determinant of a K-linear endomorphism of finite-dimensional vector space
references.reason: The determinant is a general linear-algebra object, distinct from field norm.

references.context: Field theory: multiplication endomorphism m_α:x↦αx of extension L
references.reason: This construction also appears in the trace definition.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed field trace through the trace of multiplication as a K-linear endomorphism, distinct from field norm.

references.matching_note: Field trace is defined for finite field extensions.
Multiplication by α is linear over K.

references.context: Linear algebra: trace of a K-linear endomorphism of finite-dimensional vector space
references.reason: The matrix trace is used to define the field trace.

references.context: Field theory: multiplication endomorphism of extension L considered as K-vector space
references.reason: This shares the field-norm multiplication construction.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed tensor algebra as graded sum of tensor powers with concatenation multiplication, preserving the structural algebraic prerequisites.

references.matching_note: M is a module over R.
The n-fold tensor powers iterate the module tensor product.

references.context: Graded algebra: tensor algebra with multiplication preserving nonnegative grading
references.reason: The graded algebra structure is separate from the underlying R-module.

references.context: Module theory: countable direct sum indexed by nonnegative tensor degrees
references.reason: The direct sum forms the graded module underlying tensor algebra.

references.context: Multilinear algebra: tensor concatenation product T^m(M)×T^n(M)→T^{m+n}(M)
references.reason: This is the algebra multiplication, beyond ordinary module tensor product.
